Brasília/Cuiabá: Summer Institute of Linguistics. Section 3.5 'Pankarú (Pankararú). Lista 1' (informant João Moreno, c. 50, Brejo dos Padres PE; investigator Wilbur Pickering, 1961), pp. 41-43 of the 1978 print (pp. 24-26 of the SIL reformatted PDF).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing as a rule. The only Pankararú material is an ~80-item phonetic wordlist (Parte A/B) transcribed with a stress mark ' and pitch/tone diacritics (e.g. 'žúbʌ̀ 'amarelo', 'tíŋgʌ́ 'branco', 'po 'fogo', 'žasì 'lua', 'ářà 'dia' vs. à'lų́ 'joelho', pəřə'nà 'mar', žá'gwà 'onça', pi'tų̀ 'noite', mʌ̨̀n'dī 'mandioca', sé'tį̀ 'meu nariz'); stress falls on different syllables in different items and no transcription key or comment on accent is given anywhere in the book. Introduction notes 26 of 80 items (32%) look Tupi and warns (Landerman note 2, p. 59) that the informants may have been giving Tup…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page pank1250 (refs: Fabre 2005; Ethnologue 2025 status 'Dormant'); Wikipedia (en) 'Pankararú language' and (pt) 'Língua pancararu' (raw wikitext saved).
sources.note: Glottolog lists zero descriptive references. Wikipedia only reproduces the four wordlists (Nimuendajú 1935 'Macarú' ~20 words; Pompeu 1958; Carneiro in Loukotka 1963; Meader 1978) and says nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005 [rev. 2007]. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: entry PANKARARU / PANKARARÉ (3 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; classification note (isolate; Greenberg's Macro-Tucanoan grouping on 5 supposed cognates), population, and a 50-item bibliography that is almost entirely ethnographic. Only linguistic-looking items: Meader 1978, Pompeu 1958, Loukotka 1963, Souza 1993 (Terra Indígena).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center (Pankararú entry, pp. 87-88 per Meader 1978 n. 2).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Compiles the pre-1961 Pankararú items (sol panyé, homem porkiá..) used by later classifiers; no stress statement expected, but it is the reference Glottolog-era surveys cite.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1963. Documents et vocabulaires inédits de langues et de dialectes sud-américains. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 52(1): 7-60 (Pankarurú words from the Raimundo Dantas Carneiro manuscript).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Primary wordlist not yet opened; check Loukotka's remarks on the source and whether accent is marked. Open access on Persée but the PDF download is gated by an altcha challenge by automated download.

sources.citation: Pompeu Sobrinho, Thomaz. 1958. Línguas Tapuias desconhecidas do Nordeste: Alguns vocabulários inéditos. Boletim de Antropologia (Fortaleza) 2(1): 3-19. Vocabulário nº 1 'Brejo dos Padres' (59 items, collected by Carlos Estêvão de Oliveira c. 1940), pp. 10-11; Vocabulário nº 2 (words gathered at Brejo dos Padres but attributed to 'Serra Negra' Indians), pp. 11-12; conventions p. 14.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No rule. Orthographic wordlist in which, per the stated convention (p. 14: 'Acento agudo para a tônica'), an acute accent marks the stressed syllable; the Brejo dos Padres items are mostly oxytone (obaí, jinikací, tuká, burúti, kanarí, tarací, umaiatá, tóitú) with some paroxytones (dáka, barkíra, kuriépe, ipá?). The collector himself says the list mixes Tupi, Fulniô and unknown-language words. Nothing said about accent placement as such.
